description: Edison, Wen Bin, Yucca, Xue Yuan, Isabel
summary: TOTC is a crop-rotation decision-support platform that helps durum wheat farmers in Southern Italy make informed cropping decisions amid increasingly volatile environmental conditions. The platform combines historical agricultural data and NASA satellite-derived observations to translate environmental conditions such as rainfall patterns, soil moisture availability and temperature extremes into predictive insights relevant to field-level decision-making. Our app evaluates alternative rotations involving faba beans, chickpeas and vetch across multiple economic and environmental criteria: gross cost margins, water needs, soil health and forage use. Farmers can assign different weights to these considerations according to their priorities, enabling them to compare potential trade-offs between economic returns and agricultural sustainability. The platform presents these comparisons through an interactive interface, displaying environmental information, rotation assessments and supporting evidence to make the analysis more accessible and transparent. By combining Earth observation data, agronomic knowledge and farmer-defined priorities, our app bridges the accessibility gap between satellite-derived information and practical agricultural decisions. Ultimately, we aim to support farmers in identifying cropping strategies suited to their field conditions and personal objectives, supporting more economically viable and environmentally resilient agriculture in a changing climate.
details:
What the Platform Does

github.com/wenbinio/topofthecrop

Top of the Crop is a crop-rotation decision-support platform that aims to help durum wheat farmers in Southern Italy make informed cropping decisions and stay on top of their crop yields amid increasingly variable environmental conditions. By pairing scientifically backed insights with an intuitive interface, our app makes complex agricultural data easy for every farmer to understand and use. Our project focuses on Southern Italy, particularly in areas like Basilicata, where agricultural systems are especially vulnerable to changing rainfall patterns, temperature extremes and crop diseases.

Traditionally, crop selection decisions rely heavily on farmers’ experience, local knowledge and even past farming practices. However, as climate change becomes more severe, it becomes more difficult to predict weather patterns and extreme weather events, making it difficult to determine whether continuing with the same crop or introducing alternative crops would be more beneficial.

Top of the Crop aims to address these challenges by providing a more accessible, convenient and transparent means for farmers to evaluate crop rotation decisions. By combining past environmental observations, soil information and economic considerations, the platform considers different cropping sequences and presents the best suggestion to farmers based on immediate economic returns and longer-term agricultural sustainability.

Farmers can also choose to explore alternative rotations to see potential risks and benefits, allowing them to make the final decisions based on their own personal priorities and preferences.

How it Works:

1. Earth Observation Data Integration

Top of the Crop uses Earth Observation datasets and past climate information to characterise environmental conditions across the study region. Satellite observations provide information about vegetation development, surface conditions and water availability. 

The environmental data considered include (but are not limited to):

  • ERA5-Land: Historical meteorological data used to analyse rainfall patterns and temperature conditions across the study region
  • SMAP (Soil Moisture Active Passive):  Satellite-derived soil moisture observations used to assess soil water availability and identify potential periods of water stress
  • MODIS Evapotranspiration: Satellite-derived evapotranspiration data used to examine water loss through evaporation and plant transpiration, providing additional insight into crop water dynamics.
  • Climate Projections: Future climate datasets used to investigate potential changes in environmental conditions relative to a historical baseline covering 2001–2020.
  • ISRIC Soil Information: Soil datasets used to characterise properties such as soil nitrogen and water-holding capacity, which influence nutrient availability and the ability of soils to retain water.

The following graphs were generated by us to illustrate and analyse environmental patterns in the field of interest:

*Please refer to the data sources section below for the comprehensive list.

These datasets provide complementary information about climatic conditions, water availability and soil properties, allowing Top of the Crop to assess environmental factors that influence crop suitability and agricultural productivity.

2. Field-Level Environmental Assessment

The Bradano River Basin is divided into a common 1 km spatial grid to enable consistent comparisons between datasets. Datasets are then obtained at different spatial resolutions and adjusted to maintain a consistent spatial framework.

The platform examines historical environmental observations to identify recurring patterns and variations between growing seasons. Instead of relying exclusively on long-term averages, the analysis also considers unfavourable years and environmental extremes that may affect crop development. For future climate assessment, projected environmental conditions are compared against the 2001–2020 historical baseline. This provides a reference for examining potential changes in climatic conditions and understanding how future growing environments may differ from those experienced historically.

3. Crop Rotation/Intercropping Evaluation

The main function of our app is to evaluate alternative crop rotations/intercropping plans against the existing practice of durum wheat monocultivation by Italian farms. The platform considers alternative break crops such as faba beans, chickpeas and vetch, which were assessed in rotation with durum wheat. Top of the Crop considers potential benefits and risks across rotation cycles. For example, legumes such as faba bean and chickpea can contribute to soil nitrogen through biological nitrogen fixation, potentially benefiting subsequent durum wheat crops. Break crops may also help interrupt cereal-specific pest and disease cycles. However, these benefits must be considered alongside factors such as crop water requirements, production costs and market returns.

Each rotation is assessed using several economic and environmental criteria: 

  • Economic Returns: Estimated gross margin, after variable production costs, accounting for EU support schemes and subsidies (farmers can select in the app which schemes apply to them)
  • Water Requirements: Crop water demand and environmental conditions affecting water availability
  • Soil Health and Conditions: Potential contributions to soil fertility and nitrogen
  • Forage Potential: Potential use of selected crops as animal feed

These criteria allow the platform to compare the overall performance of different rotation strategies rather than simply identifying the crop with the highest individual gross margin.

4. Farmer-Centred Interface and Decision Support

  • Field Selection and Visualisation: Farmers can manually select their field on a map, view its location and explore satellite imagery of the surrounding farmland 
  • Personalisation: Although some values in the app are auto-generated by our own online research data, farmers can edit those values to input their own crop prices, choose their priorities by ranking based on the evaluation criteria, and also customise machinery availability to have more tailored, accurate, and up-to-date recommendations for crop rotation. They are also able to save their favourite crop plans if they would like to refer to them again
  • Accessibility and Interaction: The platform includes Italian language support and speech-to-text input that makes the platform easier for local farmers to use, including those who may be less comfortable typing or navigating technical interfaces

Benefits and Goals

  • Encourages Crop Diversification: Allows farmers to explore alternatives to continuous durum wheat cultivation before executing them and provides a concise platform for them to understand potential economic and environmental benefits or risks of different crop rotations
  • User-Defined System: Allows farmers to tailor statistics based on their local farm needs and priorities. The platform also provides indicators and supporting evidence to make comparisons more transparent and allows users to understand the factors contributing to each of them
  • Sustainable Farming: By supporting more climate-informed decision-making with historical environmental data, Top Crop helps farmers consider long-term impacts and weather conditions, encouraging a more environmentally sustainable and economically viable farming system in Southern Italy

Software and Development Tools

The project uses a combination of programming languages and platforms for data processing and application development:

  • Google Earth Engine: Used to access and process satellite, climate and geospatial datasets.
  • Python: Used in the development of the environmental data-processing notebooks.
  • JavaScript: Used for application development and preparing processed data for integration into the web interface.
  • GitHub: Used to store and share the application's code, data-processing notebooks, processed datasets and documentation.
  • GitHub Pages: Used to host the web application.
dataRefs: MODIS Terra Vegetation Indices 16-Day 250 m (MOD13Q1 v6.1). Greenness: green, patchy and bare months, bare months after harvest, peak greenness, green-up and dry-off dates.
MODIS Terra Net Evapotranspiration 8-Day 500 m (MOD16A2GF v6.1; MOD16A2 for the latest months). Water the crops used each season.
GPM IMERG Final Precipitation, monthly 0.1° (V07). One of three rain sources (with CHIRPS and ERA5-Land; the app shows their median).

NASA Earth Exchange Global Daily Downscaled Projections (NEX-GDDP-CMIP6). Change by 2041–2060 from 29 climate models, middle (SSP2-4.5) and high (SSP5-8.5) emissions: hot days at flowering, daytime high, rain, frost.
SMAP L4 Global 3-hourly 9 km Surface and Root Zone Soil Moisture (SPL4SMGP v8). Root-zone soil water at sowing and in spring.
NASADEM Merged DEM Global 1 arc second (v001). Height and slope, in the data files.
Harmonized Landsat Sentinel-2 (HLSL30 and HLSS30 v2.0). 30 m greenness at the demo field, to check MODIS.
Harmonized Landsat Sentinel-2 (HLSL30 and HLSS30 v2.0). 30 m greenness at the demo field, to check MODIS.
NASA POWER, daily. Live area weather history and this season’s rain; also a rain and temperature check at the demo field.
projectRefs: Copernicus Sentinel-2 (ESA / European Union). Contains modified Copernicus Sentinel data 2016-2026.
Surface reflectance with Cloud Score+, in Google Earth Engine: 10 m greenness at the demo field (Pasquarella et al. 2023).
